newsitem.title: SPAIN: SWIMMING-KOVACS TRIUMPHS IN RIVER MARATHON.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-KOVACS TRIUMPHS IN RIVER MARATHON.

text.p: Hungary's Rita Kovacs, unfazed by the ferocious early pace set by Italian rival Valeria Casprini, prevailed in a river battle lasting more than five hours to win the women's 25-kilometre long distance race at the European swimming championships on Friday.

Kovacs, silver medallist at the 1994 world championships, did not even look out of breath as she touched at the end of a race which started in the early light of morning and finished in the boiling heat of early afternoon.
Three of the 17 starters failed to complete the gruelling event in Seville's River Guadalquivir, which world swimming's governing body wants included in the Olympics.
Casprini set off at her customary sprint tempo, with Kovacs content to allow the Italian -- and Edith van Dijk of the Netherlands -- to open up a huge lead.

Van Dijk chased 21-year-old Casprini, winner in January of a 25-km race over next year's world championship course in Perth, Australia, but Kovacs was content to bide her time during the five laps of the five-km circuit.

At 15 kms she was three minutes adrift but then she began her relentless charge, overhauling 1995 silver medallist Van Dijk on the fourth lap and picking off the brave Casprini during the 23rd kilometre.
"I thought it was so fast at the beginning. I thought it was too fast for the 25 kilometres but I trusted myself," Kovacs said after the race.
Casprini's three-minute lead did not worry her. "(I thought ) I must do it. I want to do it," she said.
"During the race I was really tired but my mind was strong."
Casprini, bronze medallist behind the victorious Kovacs in the five-kilometre event at the 1995 European championships in Vienna, said her hopes of gold evaporated when the Hungarian began her chase.
"At 15 kilometres I learned Kovacs was coming and knew I had lost. I was tired. My arms were very heavy," she said.
There was no denying Kovacs, who turned an 89-second deficit into a 90-second victory on the final lap.
Kovacs won in five hours 21 minutes 58 seconds, with Casprini taking the silver in 5:23.28 and Van Dijk the bronze in 5:25:28.
Yvette Hlavacova of the Czech Republic, third at five kms, had to give up after 18 kms after suffering from a bad stomach ache for most of the race.

British pair Sara Ward and Alix Scott also failed to finish, Ward after six kilometres because of abdomen pains and feelings of nausea and Scott soon after the halfway mark with tendinitis in her shoulder.
